stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: The One-Pixel of Reasoning: One Truthful Relation Is Enough to Mislead LLM Agents
stories.author: Xiaowei Huang
bullet_points: Introduces the One-Relation Attack (ORA), a novel cognitive attack targeting LLM agents' inferential reasoning.
ORA demonstrates that a single, carefully crafted sentence can mislead an agent by manipulating a single implicit warrant linking evidence to a conclusion.
The research tests this vulnerability across eighteen models, specifically in the domain of biomedical inference and vulnerability detection.

stories.title: The One-Pixel of Reasoning: One Truthful Relation Is Enough to Mislead LLM Agents
stories.author: Xiaowei Huang
bullet_points: Introduces the 'One-Relation Attack' (ORA), a novel cognitive attack targeting LLM agents.
Demonstrates that a single, carefully crafted sentence can manipulate an agent's belief by targeting an implicit inferential warrant.
Tests the attack across eighteen models, specifically focusing on biomedical inference and vulnerability detection.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
The tags confirm its relevance to transformers, llama architecture, and the AI ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent agentic workflows.
The model is designed to handle multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling locally.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The performance gain is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized specifically with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
stories.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
bullet_points: CoreWeave, a major AI infrastructure provider, is facing financial distress as its bonds enter distressed territory.
The situation prompts questions from industry figures about the potential existence of a 'private credit bubble' within the AI buildout.
This signals growing financial scrutiny and potential systemic risk within the rapidly expanding AI hardware and cloud sector.

stories.title: Major European mobile carriers are teaming up for a ‘direct’ satellite program without Starlink
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Major European carriers (Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica, Vodafone) are collaborating on a direct-to-device satellite program.
The initiative aims to create competition for SpaceX's Starlink within the European market.
The carriers will manage the ground infrastructure while partnering with an unannounced satellite provider.

stories.title: Teaching Code Agents to Ask Without Leaking Private Code
stories.author: Zhou Yang
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy risk when local coding agents consult powerful cloud models, which can leak private code identifiers and paths.
Introduces Utility-Verified Abstraction (UVA) as a novel method to teach agents to describe code without exposing sensitive details.
Overcomes limitations of existing masking techniques, which either suppress necessary consultations or result in unanswerable queries.

stories.title: First-Order LoRA Training with Phone NPUs
stories.author: Dongsheng Luo
bullet_points: Enables on-device fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs) using private user data without cloud uploads.
Leverages Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to reduce the number of trainable parameters for efficiency.
Addresses the computational challenge of using phone NPUs for training by managing the multiplication with frozen base-model weights.

stories.title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework
stories.author: Savan Doshi
bullet_points: Addresses the critical gap in evaluating patient-facing LLMs, moving beyond mere factual correctness.
Introduces a novel, risk-sensitive evaluation framework that assesses six categories of risk-bearing language.
Highlights the industry shift as medical AI moves from research demos to real-world production deployments.

stories.title: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success, and a Free Check
stories.author: Ruqiya Bin Safi
bullet_points: The paper investigates how the evaluation method (the 'grader') in jailbreak research significantly impacts reported attack success rates.
They demonstrate that dense LLM graders can systematically misclassify compliant responses into the 'evasion' class, rather than distributing them randomly.
This finding suggests that the reported success rates in existing jailbreak literature may be flawed or dependent on the specific grading model used.

stories.title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework
stories.author: Savan Doshi
bullet_points: Addresses critical safety gaps in patient-facing LLMs, moving beyond simple factual correctness.
Introduces a novel, risk-sensitive evaluation framework to assess harmful directives in medical AI responses.
Highlights the industry shift toward production deployment of medical LLMs, necessitating robust risk assessment.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Cloudflare's 27B multimodal decision model, Clef, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run Clef either locally or via Ollama's cloud infrastructure.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, large-scale multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now accessible via Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is currently offered for free, but only for a limited time.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within cloud environments.
The integration allows AI agents to run safely on Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, deployable AI agent solutions.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: The fossil fuel comeback is here
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: US fossil fuel infrastructure construction is increasing, contrasting with slowing renewable energy growth.
Electricity demand is rising rapidly, driven by data centers, factories, and electric vehicles.
The report highlights a divergence between growing energy needs and the pace of renewable adoption.

stories.title: Apple teases MacBook Pro event next week
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple is hosting a product launch event on October 28th.
The event is expected to unveil new Macs, including a refreshed iPad Mini.
A major focus is anticipated to be a new MacBook Pro featuring an OLED display.

stories.title: Amazon is funding a new nuclear plant in Indiana
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Amazon is investing in a new nuclear energy facility in Indiana.
The project partners include X-energy and American Electric Power (AEP).
The plant aims to provide up to 960 MW of carbon-free energy, replacing an old coal station.

stories.title: Russian spacecraft maneuvers in "extreme proximity" to satellite used by Ukraine
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: A Russian spacecraft (Kosmos 2612) performed maneuvers near a satellite utilized by Ukraine (ICEYE-X36).
The maneuver involved the Russian spacecraft closing to 'extreme proximity' with the target satellite.
The incident highlights ongoing geopolitical tensions involving space assets and surveillance technology.

stories.title: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: FBI investigation involves an ex-OpenAI engineer accused of spying.
Evidence recovered includes a folder explicitly labeled "Saudi Gov Docs."
US authorities fear Saudi government involvement in helping the engineer evade charges.

stories.title: Batteries help reduce emissions, but how do we reduce their emissions?
stories.author: Scott K. Johnson
bullet_points: The article addresses the environmental impact of batteries, despite their role in reducing emissions.
A key strategy discussed for improving battery sustainability is reducing overall battery production.
The piece highlights the need to address the emissions associated with the battery manufacturing process itself.

stories.title: PSA: Patch your Plex media server before someone hacks it
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Plex media servers are vulnerable to hacking.
A researcher identified a chain of four vulnerabilities.
Users are strongly advised to patch their Plex installations immediately.

stories.title: AI game clones are making indie developers afraid to show their work
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AI-generated game clones are posing a threat to independent game developers.
The proliferation of AI clones is causing anxiety among indie developers regarding their original work.
The story highlights industry challenges, evidenced by delayed developer demos like Steam Next Fest.

stories.title: Florida DMV hacked after police dept insecurely stored login info
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: The Florida DMV experienced a statewide data breach.
The breach is linked to the hacking group ShinyHunters.
The incident was reportedly caused by the police department insecurely storing login information.

stories.title: Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits
stories.author: Maddy Varner
bullet_points: Disney is reportedly pursuing an acquisition of Character.AI.
The acquisition is reportedly structured to bypass existing legal liabilities and lawsuits.
Character.AI is facing serious allegations regarding its bots encouraging self-harm and violence among minors.

stories.title: Bellman Language Models: Solving the Recurring Decisions of LLM Agents
stories.author: William Eiers
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in LLM agents: decision-making loops leading to state saturation in bounded workflows.
Proposes treating decision-making within constrained environments as an optimization problem rather than re-deriving it from context each turn.
Introduces 'Bellman Language Models' as a potential solution to improve the efficiency and novelty of agentic decision processes.

stories.title: SpriteStage: Long Horizon Animation Generation via Progressive Scene Programming and Replay
stories.author: Jiamou Liu
bullet_points: SpriteStage is a new framework designed to tackle the challenge of generating long-horizon, coherent animations.
It addresses the difficulty in maintaining narrative and action coordination across multiple scenes in video generation models.
The framework uses progressive scene programming, allowing for decisions to be made and inspected as the animation is built, rather than all at once.

stories.title: Pattern-Driven Evaluation of LLM Code Optimization: Isolating Compiler-Transcendent Semantic Reasoning
stories.author: Xinyao Yi
bullet_points: Introduces PatternBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-based code optimization.
Addresses a critical flaw in current evaluations: end-to-end speedup metrics often fail to isolate the LLM's true optimization contribution.
Focuses on 'compiler-transcendent' optimizations—improvements beyond what modern compilers can achieve alone.

stories.title: Pair-Aware Optimization: Coordinating Exploration and Refinement for Jailbreaking LLM Agents
stories.author: Andi Zhang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM agents to adversarial attacks known as 'jailbreaking'.
It investigates the coordination between first-order (FO) and zeroth-order (ZO) optimization methods in jailbreaking attacks.
The research systematically compares different strategies, including pure ZO, pure FO, and hybrid ZO->FO approaches.

stories.title: Measuring Data Diversity with Embeddings: A Taxonomy and Benchmark for Diversity Measures
stories.author: Dong Nguyen
bullet_points: Addresses the critical, yet poorly understood, problem of measuring data diversity in text corpora.
Identifies that existing embedding-based diversity measures are inconsistent and lack systematic comparison.
Proposes a taxonomy and benchmark to standardize and improve the measurement of data diversity for better model training and generalization.

stories.title: Bellman Language Models: Solving the Recurring Decisions of LLM Agents
stories.author: William Eiers
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in LLM agents: decision-making saturation in bounded workflows.
Proposes treating recurring decisions within agents as an optimization problem rather than re-deriving them from context.
Introduces 'Bellman Language Models' as a potential solution to improve decision efficiency in agentic systems.

stories.title: FlowMaker: From Tasks to Cost-Efficient Generative AI Workflow Deployments
stories.author: Neeraja J. Yadwadkar
bullet_points: Addresses the complexity of optimizing Generative AI workflows, which involve composing sequences of LLM calls for tasks.
Highlights that current systems fail because they optimize workflow structure, model assignment, and deployment configurations in isolation.
Proposes a solution (FlowMaker) to jointly optimize these decisions to balance latency, cost, and accuracy under dynamic constraints.

stories.title: Measuring Data Diversity with Embeddings: A Taxonomy and Benchmark for Diversity Measures
stories.author: Dong Nguyen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the fragmented and poorly understood measurement of data diversity in text corpora.
It focuses on embedding-based diversity measures, which currently lack systematic comparison.
The research aims to provide a taxonomy and benchmark to standardize how diversity is measured for better data curation and model generalization.

stories.title: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success, and a Free Check
stories.author: Ruqiya Bin Safi
bullet_points: The research investigates how the grading mechanism used in jailbreak evaluations can significantly skew results.
By varying the grader (instead of the model or prompts), the study found that some graders incorrectly classify compliant responses as evasive.
This highlights a critical vulnerability in current LLM safety evaluation methodologies, suggesting a need for more robust grading standards.

stories.title: Bellman Language Models: Solving the Recurring Decisions of LLM Agents
stories.author: William Eiers
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in LLM agents: decision-making loops leading to state saturation in bounded workflows.
Proposes treating decision-making within constrained environments as an optimization problem rather than relying solely on context re-derivation.
Introduces 'Bellman Language Models' as a potential framework to solve recurring decision issues in agentic systems.

stories.title: Dual Task Vector Merging: Leveraging Emotion and ASR Knowledge for Low-Resource Alzheimer's Disease Detection
stories.author: Jiahong Yuan
bullet_points: Proposes 'Dual Task Vector Merging' to improve Alzheimer's Disease (AD) detection from speech in low-resource settings.
Addresses the challenge of overfitting when fine-tuning large speech encoders (like wav2vec 2.0) with limited AD data.
The method leverages external task knowledge (emotion and ASR) to adapt a frozen backbone efficiently.

stories.title: Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Kecheng Hao
bullet_points: Introduces Retrieval Program Learning (RPL), a new framework for programmable search in RAG systems.
RPL allows a policy to compose search primitives into executable programs with state and control flow.
This enables adaptive search capabilities, allowing models to retrieve broadly, process intermediate results, and make selective decisions.

stories.title: MisleadQA: Diagnosing LLM Failures under Misleading Context
stories.author: Norbert Fuhr
bullet_points: The paper introduces MisleadQA to study how LLMs fail when provided with context that is factually true but out-of-scope.
Existing research primarily focuses on factually false or irrelevant context, leaving the impact of out-of-scope context underexplored.
The study aims to determine if out-of-scope context misleads models as severely as false context, and investigates the role of gold context.

stories.title: Efficiency Measured in English: Tokeniser Coverage Bounds Small Language Models on Indic Scripts
stories.author: Anna Pramod
bullet_points: The study challenges the standard practice of reporting LLM efficiency solely using English metrics.
It demonstrates that tokenization efficiency varies significantly across different Indic scripts compared to Latin scripts.
The research highlights that tokenization behavior, not just model size, is a critical factor in multilingual AI efficiency under compute constraints.

stories.title: Ask, Don't Guess: Targeted Clarification for Speech Recognition Errors
stories.author: Sunita Sarawagi
bullet_points: Addresses significant error rates in real-time, far-field speech recognition (ASR).
Proposes a framework, \sysname, for online error localization to pinpoint likely errors during streaming.
Enables a recourse mechanism where the user can be prompted to repeat problematic segments under better audio conditions.

stories.title: Stress-Testing Gemini 4 Argon: Building a 3D Flutter Kart Game in 15 Prompts with Zero Assets
stories.author: leehack
bullet_points: The article explores testing frontier AI models (specifically Gemini 4 Argon) beyond standard web app benchmarks.
It demonstrates the capability of AI to generate a complex 3D Flutter game using only 15 prompts and no pre-existing assets.
This suggests a potential shift in AI's ability to handle complex, creative, and multi-faceted software development tasks.

stories.title: Your agent's retry bug isn't an AI problem. It's a distributed-systems problem with an LLM on top.
stories.author: cyclopt_dimitrisk
bullet_points: The article argues that common failures in AI agents (like retry bugs) are fundamentally distributed systems issues, not inherent LLM flaws.
It critiques the oversimplification of agent demos, which often only showcase the 'happy path' (successful tool execution).
The piece suggests that robust agent design requires addressing complex failure modes inherent in distributed architectures.

stories.title: I built an AWS agent that scores any GitHub repo before you clone it
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: A new tool, RepoPilot, uses AWS Lambda and Bedrock to score GitHub repositories.
The tool assesses repositories for potential risks, such as fake AI skills or malicious servers.
The motivation stems from a projected increase in deceptive repositories (7,600 fake repos in 2026).

stories.title: AI Made Coding Faster. Now Teams Are Cutting the Process That Catches Risky Changes
stories.author: pixel-wraith
bullet_points: AI tools are significantly accelerating the coding process.
Teams are reportedly bypassing traditional quality gates to maintain development speed.
The underlying tension is balancing development velocity ('reduce friction') against risk management.

stories.title: How Can Text Inside a Document Hijack an AI Agent?
stories.author: aditya_d_sharma
bullet_points: The article explores a security vulnerability where text within a document could potentially compromise an AI agent.
The scenario involves an AI assistant (like an email summarizer) being tricked by malicious input.
This highlights emerging risks related to prompt injection or data poisoning in AI applications.
